verdicts.reason: Requirement is stated by the quote (OI-002), but it is an open item and the requirement is on the clock controller's behaviour; not checkable from the bridge interface in a scenario as a clean check. Actor is the system/clock controller, scenario is plausible. Keep the fields but the rule is acceptable as a scenario with gated clock.

Quote states the requester follows APB: setup then access until PREADY, stable fields, PSTRB low in read. These are checkable every cycle from interface signals (assumption on the requester), so check should be assertion; actor master is right.
Assumption that the clock controller keeps i_clk_slv running while a request is in flight; external to the bridge, nothing to check on the DUT. check=none is right.
Architecture decision (handshake instead of async FIFO); a description of the design with nothing to verify or exercise directly. Behaviour is covered by the handshake rules.

Parameter selecting APB4/APB5 with PWAKEUP and user signals and no parity signals is a configuration description; it can be exercised in scenarios by building both configurations. Rule is stated, but strength is a decision statement ('shall'), keep MUST scenario.
Parameter defaults and ranges are stated by the quote; exercised by configuration scenarios.

Quote says APB outputs are flip-flop outputs and PREADY high only in state RESP. Flip-flop output is structural, but PREADY only after Access phase is reached is checkable from interface signals (PREADY implies PSEL and PENABLE). Actor is the bridge on the APB side, a slave/completer, correct. Check should be both: assertion for PREADY only in Access, structural part not checkable.
Four-phase handshake: response delivered only after the handshake closed; checkable by assertion and scenario. Actor system (bridge internal handshake) is acceptable.
RTL top declares APB5 ports in every configuration, with min widths 1, unused inputs ignored, unused outputs 0; exercised by scenarios across configurations.

questions.question: OI-002/ASM-005: Which party guarantees the slv clock is running when a request arrives with a gated clock enabled only by PWAKEUP? It is an open item for the designer to clarify.
DEC-019 and DEC-020 are the author's choices and not confirmed by the designer. Should PREADY-only-in-RESP and response-after-handshake-closed be treated as binding for verification?
DEC-021 deviates from PRT-03 by declaring APB5 ports in all configurations. Does the designer accept this deviation, and does it conflict with the APB4 configuration in DEC-003?
